steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: You've been tampering with the locks again. You just won't give up, will you?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Unfortunately, the area that the search parties are looking is at least five kilometers from here. Don't expect them to hear your distress signal.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: At least eat something.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Malnutrition during the recovery process will increase the time needed for bones to mend by twenty percent, and the chance of complications by thirty-five percent.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: It's not my intention to hurt you, or leave an outstanding warrior with a permanent disability.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Cut the crap!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I warn you, you'd better kill me now...

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: I suppose that's an option...

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: As I said, however, I have no intention of bringing harm to Kjerag, and I certainly feel no need to take innocent Kjerag lives.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Besides, it was a miracle that we survived that avalanche at all...

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: It was, in your people's words, 'Kjeragandr's protection'. Right?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Shouldn't that be a sign to a faithful follower of Kjeragandr to value her own life?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: No intention of bringing harm to Kjerag? You've been spying for the Victorians and stealing Kjerag's military secrets!

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Such an unfair accusation.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Do you really think a few battleships constitute Kjerag's most important secret?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: You speak of your god's blessings all the time, but have you really thought about what your god is?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: What are you talking about... Kjeragandr is not to be questioned or doubted—

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: That didn't resonate? Well... I guess the only reason I'm talking to you about this is because there's nothing to do here to pass the time.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Ah well, doesn't matter anyway.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: If you want to pass the time, I've got something to ask you.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: How did a Victorian spy work for Rhine Lab for so long?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Why are you so sure that I'm a Victorian spy, when I've been working at Rhine Lab for so long?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Well... if you really want to hear it, I could tell you a little story—

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: There was once a girl in Victoria, who was incredibly fascinated to know how everything worked, and she wanted to spend her whole life studying.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: A dozen years later, she went to Columbia as visiting scholar from the Royal Victorian Academy of Sciences...

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: It was not the research foundations of Victoria that found her, but an intelligence agency.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: From that day forth, the only thing she was allowed to be curious about was the secret documents of the Columbian government.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: But her curiosity was not so easily stated. As she dug through Columbia's secrets, she found an opportunity to satisfy the very depths of her curiosity...

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: At the end of the day, though, there is little that separates Columbia and Victoria.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: People fight over the slightest morsel of profit, the order that took so much hard work to build is now teetering on the brink of ruinous war...

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Who has the time to gaze up at the heavens... or even down at the ground we stand on, of which we know so little about?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: ...I find it all a tedious bore.
Early morning, Hall of Writings, Vine-Bead Court.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Good thing the window isn't too high.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: The clerics have gone to their morning prayers... the observation station is a sensitive topic right now. I need to avoid them.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Maps, geographical records... anything that can help...
The morning sun shines through the window, and falls gently on the aged books.
Elena dusts off the books in front of her, but finds the writing of the clerics difficult to decipher. She begins to regret not bringing a dictionary of the Kjeragi language.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: How do they categorize this stuff? This one's... a collection of quotes?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: 'Kjeragandr, showed Herself, to me, and said—'
'Seek not my temple, but my heart.'

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Whoa—!
Elena lets go in panic, and the heavy book hits the floor.
Through the bookshelves, she sees a surprised face under a hood, and a crossbow pointed at her face.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: I think she's surrendering, Enya. What do we do?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Who's saying anything about surrendering?!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Wait a moment... Enya? Enya Silverash?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Y-You're the Saintess?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Shh—
Elena nods in realization.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Keep quiet, and we can talk. Alright?
Elena nods carefully.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Put away your crossbow, Joanna. Let's not scare our friend here.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: But she sneaked into the Vine-Bead Court. Doesn't seem like something a good person would do.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Well, we sneaked in too...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Your attire... are you from Rhine Lab?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Yes! I'm Elena, a researcher in the Energy Section.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I'm sorry. I was just looking for a map of Kjerag, preferably recording the locations of mountains and Originium veins...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: If I find that special vein, maybe I could—

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...You could what?
Elena glances at the young woman before her, who looks about the same age as her, while being the undisputed sovereign of this country.
Elena is unsure if what she is about to say might offend her, but when she sees the pure curiosity on her face...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Maybe... I can explain how this Catastrophe happened!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: You mean that Kjerag has been safe from Catastrophe for a thousand years because of a hidden Originium vein?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Yes! There is an undiscovered Originium vein in the mountains surrounding Kjerag, which created an energy field that prevented Catastrophes from forming.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Impossible! It's Kjeragandr that protects Kjerag!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Has anyone ever seen Kjeragandr with their own eyes?

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Many people have witnessed the miracles of Kjeragandr with their own eyes!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I respect your culture and traditions, but that doesn't prove anything.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Just because you see something that can't be explained right now doesn't prove the existence of some supernatural being behind it.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: And how do you prove the veins have anything to do with it?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: The interactions between Originium is extremely complex, and what we know is only the tip of the iceberg.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Rhine Lab has conducted a number of experiments in recent years.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Under certain conditions, Originium can form energy fields that cause atmospheric Originium particles to disperse rather than converge, preventing the formation of Catastrophes.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: This is something that we have not yet been able to recreate under controlled conditions...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: But if an Originium vein with the right conditions exists... then preventing Catastrophe may be a real possibility.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I've made detailed calculations—

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Excuse me, can I borrow this map?

Elena takes out her notebook and show it to the other two. She goes on a long explanation about the formulas as she draws on the page, not paying attention to whether her listeners are able to keep up.
Finally, Elena confidently draws a circle at a location in the foothills on the map.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: ...Therefore, the Originium Vein Theory is the most likely explanation for Kjerag's lack of Catastrophes!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I'm quite sure that my calculations are accurate, and if we find an Originium vein at this location, it would explain everything!
Joanna is in a daze. She glances at Enya, hoping the Saintess will rebuke this blasphemy.
But the Saintess is quiet, biting her lower lip lightly.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: (Whispers) Say something! I don't know what the hell she's writing!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: How do you explain the recent Catastrophe, then?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Based on the data, I suspect something from beyond the Starpod fell on Mount Karlan the day before the Catastrophe.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Look! These are the data that the station observed the day before the Catastrophe. These are infrasound waves created by the impact of the extraterrestrial object.
Elena turns on her portable terminal, displaying a sharp break on the line graph.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: This object must be massive in size and scale. I think the Catastrophe was caused by it falling onto the central area of the vein, causing a shift in the energy field!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: There are reasons for all these things! It's not magic, or the work of a god!
Enya cannot comprehend what she is hearing. Her memory begins to blur, and she feels a sort of link being torn apart.
'Kjarr.'
A familiar voice, belonging to a friend, a miracle, or... a hallucination?
She can't believe it. She must not. Fear and loneliness comes over her, and it is all she could do to keep her arms from trembling.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Say something, Enya...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I... I can understand Elena's position.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: However, I recall a section of the Kjeragandr...

spans.text: However, I recall a section of the

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: 'Her heart is the heart of Karlan, deep within the mountains. From the beating of Her heart grew the flesh and bones of Kjerag.'

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: This is the description of the origins of Kjerag, as the scriptures record.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: We used to assume that the Heart of Karlan was Lake Silberneherze, which was why we built Kjeragandr's statue there.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: In my studies these past several days, however, I found that the ancient tomes considered the freezing of the Heart of Karlan to be an unusual phenomenon. But Lake Silberneherze freezes every year...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Sounds like a figure of speech...

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Don't interrupt the Saintess while she's thinking!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Maybe the Heart of Karlan actually refers to something else...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: The Great Elder guided me to the 'Radsorn', but it is in fact the 'Heart of Karlan' that holds the answer...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: You mentioned the central area of this 'special vein'?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Yes! I built a model based on the shape of Kjerag's mountains, and I calculated that the extraterrestrial object likely fell on...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: this location.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Isn't this.... the Kjerag-Kazimierz mines?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Mines? Yes! Now it all makes sense!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: There's no time to waste! We need to go—

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: One moment, foreigner! We didn't say anything about letting you around Kjerag on your own, not to mention all the disrespect you've shown to Kjeragandr—

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: It's alright, Joanna.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: We don't force our faith onto others. Besides, we need to find the truth behind this Catastrophe... we'll let her travel with us.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Elena...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Hm?
While Enya and Joanna were talking, Elena put the books back on the shelf, and now sits on the window sill, waving at the other two.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Actually, there's usually no one at the main entrance to the Hall of Writings.
Cold moonlight pours through the dark clouds upon the decorations in Ratatos's room.
Sciurus thought she would be afraid to see Ratatos's things, but she feels so tired that she does not even have the strength for sorrow.
She knows full well that she simply imitated Ratatos in dealing with the other clans, a few days ago.
But the more she tries, the more Ratatos's shadow lingers.
Sciurus looks outside. It seems snow is once again falling on Browntail land.

a.text: 'Look, Sciurus. Do this to the snowball, and it'll go even further when you throw it. Try it.'
'I don't need you to teach me...'
'I hate you. I hate everything you make me do.'

steps.text: The echoes of memory are like the deafening roar of a mountain collapsing. She feels a lump in her chest.
The dust-covered contracts and letters in the box bear witness to the development of Clan Browntail over the years.
Sciurus examines the marks left behind by Ratatos on the family's business documents, and finds, at the bottom of each page, where the name of the Browntail matriarch should be—
'Sciurus'

a.text: 'I'm your older sister, and I'll become the leader of Clan Browntail. So you need to listen to me.'
'Prove that you can do better, if you're not happy about that.'
'I hope you'll carry the future of Clan Browntail on your shoulders.'

steps.text: Sciurus anxiously flips through the pages.
But each and every document has her name on it.
Until she reaches the bottom of the pile, that little box from her memory—
The secret that belongs to the two of them.

a.text: 'This holds all the things that I want to give you, but don't want the adults to see.'
'A secret between the two of us, you and me.'

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: This is...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: A communicator?
Sciurus gazes at the device in her hand, the dim light illuminating her hesitation.
The final audio log...
I got Karlan Trade's intel about the suspicious woman. I've been watching her all morning, and I think she's planning to make a run for it.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: This voice... it's Monch?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Good. Keep a close eye on her. Don't let her get away, or pass the documents to anyone else.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Yes, ma'am... Karlan Trade says we need to be careful and not draw attention.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Take her alive, if possible. There are a lot of questions we need to ask her.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I'll tell Enciodes to send help from Karlan Trade.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Understood. I'll do my best.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Be careful, and don't leave loose ends.
Finally, there is an unanswered call from Karlan Trade.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Call time... yesterday?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: ...Karlan Trade?
